newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian paper sees no progress on Israel front.
newsitem.headline: Syrian paper sees no progress on Israel front.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper said on Friday there was nothing new to encourage Syria to resume peace talks with Israel.

"In light of the current practices of the Netanyahu government, which is rejecting the priciple of withdrawal from the Golan, there is nothing that Syria would negotiate for, and there is nothing which encourages her or motivates her to return to the negotiating table," al-Thawra said.

Syria has condemned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to trade occupied Arab lands for peace and says it will not hold talks with his government until he agrees to a full withdrawal from the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in 1967.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but the negotiations have been blocked over the fate of the Golan. Talks broke off in March last year.
The Syrian newspaper's comments came two days after Israel agreed to hand over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

"Land remains the element which could never be an issue for flexibility. Its full return in accordance with U.N. resolutions and the U.S. peace initiative is a condition for peace which could never be replaced," al-Thawra said.
"We are committed to peace which is still our strategic option. This peace should be based on U.N. resolutions. Any other talk is rejected and does not concern us," al-Thawra said.
